podcast.body: This song was an actual hit for Heart, reaching number 11 on the Hot 100 in 1977. While it sounded like a "screed against a snake in the grass ex-lover" on the radio, lead singer Ann Wilson actually wrote it as a diss against Heart's former label, Mushroom Records. The label had notoriously attempted to promote Ann and her sister Nancy Wilson as an "incestuous lesbian couple." "Barakuda reached number 11 on the Hot 100 in 1977."

podcast.body: Written by Ann Wilson in response to extreme sexualization by their label, Mushroom Records, and an intrusive question from a radio promoter. The label took out a full-page ad in Rolling Stone magazine with a suggestive caption under an album cover featuring the sisters with bare shoulders. The song's lyrics, "You lying so low in the weeds that you're going to ambush me, you'd have me down, down, down to my knees, wouldn't you, Barakuda?" were directed at her record label. It was released on the 1977 album `Lil' Queen` but never became a top 10 hit. "Barakuda from the 1977 album Lil Queen, which somehow never became a top 10 hit."
